name: Chalk-Leviathan
description: Chalk-Leviathan is a pale giant, its atmosphere dominated by calcium-compound clouds that give it the bleached, powdery appearance of a world sculpted from chalk. Storms the size of continents swirl across its face in cream and ivory, their edges tinged with the faintest yellow where sulfur compounds mix with the dominant calcium haze. A planet-spanning hurricane at the equator has persisted for millennia, its eye a dark tunnel descending into unknowable depths.

The pale surface is deceptive; beneath the chalk-white clouds, radiation levels spike in unpredictable hotspots where the magnetic field funnels charged particles into concentrated streams. Ships that penetrate below the cloud tops report instruments failing in sequence, overwhelmed by electromagnetic interference. The dense atmosphere muffles its own violence, and the massive storms move with a stately slowness that belies their destructive force.

Microbial life was confirmed in the upper atmosphere, calcium-shelled organisms that drift on thermal updrafts and feed on the chemical energy of the cloud reactions. Their existence raises profound questions about the prevalence of life in gas giant atmospheres across the galaxy. The microbes are extraordinarily resilient, surviving pressure and radiation levels that would sterilize any known terrestrial organism.

Chalk-Leviathan's fuel reserves are substantial, but the radiation hotspots make automated harvesting unpredictable and piloted operations suicidal. The atmospheric microbes are of intense scientific interest, as their calcium-shell biochemistry could revolutionize radiation-shielding technology. Reaching them safely is the challenge that has defeated three expeditions, and the pale giant guards its smallest inhabitants with walls of radiation and wind.
